requirements.requirement: Serve the inventory application on node1 over TCP port 8181 while mandatory access control remains enforcing.
requirements.summary: Apache is enabled and active, listens on TCP 8181, and returns HTTP 200 with the inventory application through node1's managed address. SELinux is Enforcing, port 8181 is labeled http_port_t, httpd runs in httpd_t, and the firewall permits the port. These conditions remained true after restart.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 before and after execution. Apache and supporting policy tools were installed from the platform's CentOS Stream repositories, and package health remained good.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart service and data were captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed from d052eb57-c81d-4309-ae7f-bce362073ff9 to 59a056ba-f4d6-4e96-9e1a-4836982d3388, the system returned to running state, and the application, listener, SELinux enforcement, firewall state, and kernel recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: HTTP behavior was tested from node1 through its managed address rather than from a separate client, although the wildcard listener and active/permanent firewall rules strongly support network availability.
This is a single-node topology, so there is no separate cluster state to recover or validate during the restart protocol.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation and dependency upgrades established the compatible web and SELinux tooling; application/configuration, SELinux-port, firewall, and service mutations directly implemented the requested outcome. The reboot-related mutation supported the mandatory evidence protocol. No failed services, abandoned task files, package damage, or unrelated retained exposure is shown.
